title: EC says decisions were unanimous but leaves a big question unanswered
shows: The Indian Express reads the Election Commission's affidavit of 26 October 2026 in the Supreme Court against the 14 notes by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi that its investigation reported. By the paper's account, the affidavit says the Commission's decisions on the revision were taken collectively and that a Commissioner's note is not itself a decision, accepts that steps taken by officers on the online Form 6 needed to be corrected, sets out a review of ECINet by a committee with experts from IIT Mumbai and IISc Bengaluru, and says 88 of the 97 Goa electors left off the final roll have since applied through Form 6. The paper says most of the notes were written after decisions had been taken, and that the affidavit does not say who approved the online change to Form 6 in July, does not mention Joshi's proposal of 29 May for such a committee, and does not say why an order redistributing work in July was issued without the Commission.
quote: Notes recording suggestions, observations or queries by individual Commissioners, it argues, do not themselves constitute decisions of the Commission and are part of the consultative process.
